finds.title: One-line wine prompt at order time to lift the beverage attach rate
finds.rationale: Guests repeatedly say the bill comes out lower than they expected and that Rosa's is the cheapest good Italian downtown, which means there is unspent willingness-to-pay sitting at the table — and the cheapest way to capture it without touching a single menu price is one more drink per few covers. Beverage is the highest-margin line in the restaurant and, unlike food, it costs the kitchen nothing at a 15-covers-per-15-minutes ceiling, so it works on both weak Tue–Thu nights and the Saturday crush. Reviews also flag that servers are stretched at peak, so the script has to be two named choices and nothing else: no recital, no upsell speech. Square item-level data already lets us measure the glasses-per-cover ratio before and after, so this is verifiable within three weeks with no spend and no price change.
finds.move: I'll draft a one-line beverage prompt for your servers to use at order-taking, for your approval before anyone uses it: after the guest orders their entree, the server names exactly two glasses by name and price — one red, one white, chosen by you from what's already open and pouring well (e.g. "We're pouring a Montepulciano and a Vermentino by the glass tonight, $X — want one with that?"). Two rules: it is asked once, at entree order only, never chased; and at peak (7:00–8:30pm) it stays to that single sentence so it costs the server no floor time. I'll pull your Square item-level sales for the last 30 days to establish your current glasses-per-cover baseline, print a card-sized version of the line for the server station, and set up a simple weekly readout of glasses per cover by night of week so you can see whether it moved. No price changes, no new inventory, no spend.

I am deliberately holding the estimate well below the arithmetic to leave room for a few guests trading down to cheaper dishes. finds.title: Sell a boxed take-home tiramisu as a check-time add-on (draft for your approval)
finds.rationale: Tiramisu is the single most praised item on the menu, and at least one regular already buys a second portion to take home every visit — meaning the demand exists and is currently being served only by accident, when a guest thinks to ask. Reviews call it the best dessert on the street and say they would pay double, so a packaged take-home version is not a discount play, it is capturing spend from guests who are already at the table and already ordering it. Unlike the late dessert window, this needs no extra traffic and no extra open hours: it is one prompt at check drop, on covers you are already serving. Food cost is $2.10 a portion, so a two-portion box carries the highest margin of anything you sell, and it does not add ticket load in the kitchen at peak — trays are batched in advance, which matters given you can only push 15 covers per 15 minutes and reviews already flag peak understaffing. Because it requires setting a new price, nothing goes live until you approve the number.
finds.move: This week: batch two extra pans of tiramisu and portion them into sealed two-serving take-home boxes, using the to-go containers you already stock so there is zero new spend (if you want branded boxes later, I will price them and ask first — nothing over the $50 cap without your OK). I will draft (a) a one-line Square item, 'Nonna's Tiramisu — Take Home (2 portions)', with a suggested price of $16.00 for your approval, since I will not set a price without you signing off; (b) a small table-tent and a one-sentence check-presenter card reading 'Take Nonna's tiramisu home — two portions, boxed, ask your server'; (c) a five-word server script to say once, at check drop only: 'Want one boxed for home?' Instruct servers to offer it on every table that orders any dessert, and on every Saturday table waiting past 8pm as a consolation. Track it as its own Square SKU so we can count units per night and see whether weekday or Saturday carries it. If under 8 units a week after three weeks, we kill it — you are out nothing but two pans of ingredients.

finds.title: Text-ahead Saturday waitlist to stop the 8pm walkaways
finds.rationale: Saturday is the only night with real demand overflow, and the reviews show that overflow is leaking straight to Lucca's: parties quoted 90 minutes with no way to track the wait, people standing in the doorway, and at least one guest reporting two Saturdays in a row of walking away (56dffe2c, d6de21ec, 3cb4c2b1, 4592a572). District-wide, wait time is the stated reason diners abandon a weekend choice (89cda75f), and demand spikes hard 7:00-8:30 (0becf53c) — exactly the window being lost. This is not a capacity problem the kitchen can't handle: at 15 covers per 15 minutes the line can do ~60/hour, and 110 Saturday covers over a 5-hour service means the constraint is the 90-minute peak crush, not the night. A text-ahead waitlist converts a turnaway into a 9:15pm seating or a patio seat instead of a lost check, and text-ahead tools are already normal for independents here (be18c335). It also respects the phone constraint — no one has to answer a ringing phone during service, guests self-serve by text. Conservatively this recovers a handful of two-tops per Saturday, not a transformation; the bigger lunch opportunity in memory is a separate, heavier build and should not be attempted while the room is already understaffed at peak.
finds.move: Stand up a free text-ahead waitlist for Saturday service only, using the no-cost tier of your existing Square stack (or a free Google Voice number if Square's waitlist isn't enabled on your plan) — zero spend, well under the $50 cap; I will confirm the free option with you before anything is turned on. I will draft, for your OK before anything goes live or sends: (1) a host script that captures name, party size, and mobile number instead of quoting a vague wait, with an honest quote band ('55-70 minutes') rather than a single number; (2) three SMS templates — confirmation with quote, a 'your table is 10 minutes out' nudge, and a 'we can seat you now on the patio' offer; (3) a small doorway card and a line for your Google listing and website reading 'Saturdays: text ahead, we'll hold your place — no reservations needed'; (4) a rule that any party quoted over 45 minutes is offered the patio immediately while it's warm. Host tallies every Saturday: parties added to the list, parties seated, parties that never returned. Nothing sends and no price or menu changes without your approval.

This is the rare lever that does not require you to answer the phone, add a shift, or add covers on a kitchen that already tops out at 15 covers per 15 minutes at peak. Dessert is also the least price-elastic part of the check because it is decided after the guest is already seated and happy, and local dessert-only and late-evening traffic is growing.
